subject: Capacity fit: mapping workload to GPU tiers & pricing options
messages:
From: Henry Chu <henry@medalytics.co>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity request + workload summary

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Medalytics is excited about Redwood's latency and cost story. The leadership team asked me to get you a concrete workload brief so we can understand dedicated pricing / reserved commit options. High-level footprint below; I've attached a CSV with samples and a small set of realtime traces.

- Monthly API calls (endpoints hitting generation): ~120,000 calls/month
- Average prompt length: 150 tokens (user + system)
- Average completion length: 450 tokens
- Peak concurrent requests: ~250 (peaks at PST business hours)
- Typical response P95 latency target: 250ms end-to-end
- Model mix: 70% rw-medium-v2 (latency-sensitive), 30% rw-large-v1 (higher quality)
- Growth expectation: +30% ARR cadence next 12 months, but procurement wants a 12-month committed pricing baseline

Questions for you: what GPU pool sizing do you recommend for their workload to hit the 250ms p95 target? How do you model burst capacity versus committed capacity? Please include pricing tiers (12 vs 24 month) and an example monthly commit you think is realistic.

Attachments: medalytics_request_summary.csv, poa_workload_samples.json

Henry
Head of ML — Medalytics
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Henry Chu <henry@medalytics.co>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request + workload summary

Hi Henry — thanks for the detailed brief and the sample traces. Looping in Karthik and Steph from Solutions; below is a quick acknowledgement and a short list of clarifying questions so our sizing recommendation is accurate. We should be able to get an initial draft proposal by Friday.

Quick clarifying asks:
- Are the 250 concurrent requests sustained (steady-state) or short bursts (minutes)?
- Do you have a distribution of prompt+completion lengths (we got averages, samples help but we need percentiles)?
- Is any of this PII-sensitive (affects Private deployment and encryption/KMS asks)?

High level note: for mixed-model workloads we typically size for the latency-sensitive model (rw-medium-v2) and provide a model-mix plan (dedicated pool plus a small shared fallback) so quality-heavy requests can spill to higher-capacity instances during non-peak windows.

We received the CSV and traces — Karthik, Steph: want to run quick throughput calculations and propose two commit options (conservative vs aggressive) and a burst-credit model for Medalytics. I'll synthesize and send to Henry once you both confirm numbers.

Olga
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request + workload summary — initial sizing & pricing options

Olga / Steph — ran the workload samples through our sizing model and sketched three option tiers. Notes / assumptions up front: tokenization average matches your samples (600 tokens total per request), p95 target = 250ms for rw-medium-v2, we assume typical batching 8-12 tokens per request at runtime and KV caching for repeat prefixes (expected 15% token savings). Peak concurrency 250 sustained for 10-30 minute windows. Pricing below is list MSRP converted to monthly commit for a 12-month term; discounts apply per option as noted.

Sizing assumptions & math (summary):
- Effective tokens per request (after caching): 510 tokens average
- Avg tokens/sec per request at 250ms p95: 2,040 tokens/sec equivalent for 250 concurrent requests; peak 250 concurrently -> ~510k tokens/sec? (see detailed table in internal playbook)
- We approximate throughput per L4-like instance: ~18k tokens/sec for rw-medium-v2 under optimized runtime; A100-80GB node: ~42k tokens/sec for the larger model; these are ballpark but account for KV cache overhead.

Option A — Conservative (high headroom)
- Pool: 8 x L4-equivalent GPUs (dedicated) configured with continuous batching and prefix cache
- Expected steady throughput: ~144k tokens/sec; accommodates peaks with margin; latency p95 expected < 200ms for rw-medium-v2
- 12-month commit: $145,000 / month (list); proposed customer price: $116,000 / month (20% off)
- Burst credits: additional 30% burst capacity for 6 hours/day (banked credits for seasonal spikes)

Option B — Balanced (recommended)
- Pool: 5 x L4-equivalent GPUs + 1 x A100-80GB for rw-large-v1 offload (hybrid pool)
- Expected steady throughput: ~110k tokens/sec with targeted offload for 30% heavy-model traffic
- 12-month commit: $105,000 / month (list); proposed customer price: $84,000 / month (20% off)
- Burst credits: 20% banked burst capacity, flexible burst window of up to 12 hours/month

Option C — Lean (lower commitment, more shared fallback)
- Pool: 3 x L4-equivalent GPUs dedicated; remainder runs on reserved shared capacity with automated fallback to hosted models when capacity hits SLO thresholds
- Expected steady throughput: ~60-70k tokens/sec; latency target met for 80% of traffic, fallback for large completions
- 12-month commit: $62,000 / month (list); proposed customer price: $55,800 / month (10% off)
- Burst credits: limited (10%) with higher overage rates

Commercial notes:
- 24-month commitment gives an additional 8% list discount (stackable with early-closing credits)
- We bill commits monthly; unused burst credits roll for 90 days
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated; throughput SLAs priced as part of premium SLA add-on

Attachments: pricing_term_sheet_v1.pdf (I attached the line items)

If this looks reasonable I'll draft a short MAD (mutual action plan) to send to Henry with two preferred options (Balanced + Lean) and an ask for a procurement timeline.

—Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Henry Chu <henry@medalytics.co>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medalytics.co
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request + workload summary

Olga — appreciate the rapid turnaround and the crisp options. A few questions / counter-proposals from the procurement and infra teams:

1) Can we move Option B to a lower starting commit for the first 3 months and then step up (a ramp)? Procurement wants a 3-month trial payment of 50% commit then full commit starting month 4.
2) Can you increase burst credits during our peak windows (PST mornings) to 40% for the first 60 days? That would help us avoid a big initial commit.
3) Procurement asks for a 10% overall discount on the customer price (net price) for the 12-month term in exchange for a 30-day early payment term and a case study after 9 months.

Also attaching a short POA and the sample traces (poa_workload_samples.json) for your infra team to validate the peak math. Our legal will need a short SOW & payment terms doc to start procurement.

Attachments: poa_workload_samples.json

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if useful.

Henry
Head of ML — Medalytics
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Henry Chu <henry@medalytics.co>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request + workload summary — negotiation path

Henry / Team — thanks, appreciate the flexibility. Internal note to align on path:

- We can accept the ramp structure for Option B: months 1-3 at 50% commit, month 4+ at full commit (same final price) provided we include a midterm performance review (end of month 3) and a telemetry export to validate utilization.
- Burst credits: approve temporary 40% burst for first 60 days, then drop to the standard 20% unless metrics justify extension.
- Commercial discount: I can approve a 10% additional net concession on the Balanced option (final customer price $75,600/month) in exchange for: 30-day early payment, a public case study after 9 months (commensurate marketing sign-off), and a standard playbook for operations runbook handoff.

Next steps: Karthik / Steph, please update the term sheet (pricing_term_sheet_v1.pdf) to reflect: the ramp schedule, burst-credit window, the $75,600/month net price for balanced option, and a simple SOW template for procurement. Legal: prepare a short SOW + payment terms (30-day net). Henry — once we have the updated term sheet I'll send a redline-friendly DocuSign link; you can route that to procurement.

Olga
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
